HG15-p9e2.was_md: What is the difference between a human doer and a human being? If you don’t feel good enough as a human being, you will try to become good enough as a human doer by for example being beautiful, doing something well, being smart, having a certain status, being spiritual, etc. Those can all be real gifts. They become a bargain for belonging when failing in these areas feels like losing yourself.
HG15-p9e2.new_md: What is the difference between a human doer and a human being? If you don’t feel good enough as a human being, you will try to become good enough as a human doer by for example being beautiful, doing something well, being smart, having a certain status, being spiritual, etc. I’m not saying those can’t be real gifts, but if failing at one of them feels like losing yourself, then you’re using it to buy belonging.

HG35-forgive-e3.was_md: We can not ‘force’ forgiveness on ourselves, it has to come from a place of understanding otherwise it can be bypassing. However, if we remain in the anger forever, we are allowing the injury to dictate how we live our lives in the present. So how do we hold all of this? We simply remember that it can all be true: the harm happened, the boundary still matters, the person is still accountable, and forgiveness may come later on its own.
HG35-forgive-e3.new_md: We can not ‘force’ forgiveness on ourselves, it has to come from a place of understanding otherwise it can be bypassing. However, if we remain in the anger forever, we are allowing the injury to dictate how we live our lives in the present. So how do we hold all of this? We just remember that it can all be true at once. They really did hurt us and they still have to answer for it, and our boundary with them still matters, but one day we may find that we have forgiven them.
